chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Ruh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said:

I had a female slave whom I had sexual relations with; then I had relations with her again, and sold her. She gave birth to a boy at her owner's house. They brought him to me, and they argued with me, saying, 'He is yours.' So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me, 'Accept him.'

key_terms.أَطَأُهَا: I had sexual relations with her (specifically in the context of slavery)

ai.seo_question: Who owns the child born to a female slave after her male owner sells her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *luhq al-walad* (linking offspring to the father) in the context of *ummahat al-walad* (mother of the child) within Shia jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the dispute by instructing the seller to accept the child, affirming that the child's lineage follows the father who had sexual relations with her, even after her sale. This ruling underscores the stability of family lineage and the legal status of concubinage in classical Islamic law.
